The Willys-Overland MB US Army Jeep and the Ford GPW were manufactured from 1941 to 1945. These small four-wheel drive utility vehicles are considered the iconic World War II Jeep. Willys initially won the contract to supply the war dept with Jeeps but the demand was so great, Ford was asked to produce them as well. During World War II, Willys produced 363,000 Jeeps and Ford some 280,000. Willys won the rights to continue using the Jeep name after the war, hence the CJ Jeep.

Engine; 54 hp 134 cu in Side Valve 4 cyl, 3 spd manual with 2 spd transfer case and selectable 4WD

Includes bibliographic references and index
This final environmental impact statement/proposed resource management plan amendment describes the environmental effects of two proposals by Thompson Creek Mining Company: 1) a modified mining plan of operations (MMPO) for the Thompson Creek Molybdenum Mine near the City of Clayton in Custer County, Idaho; and 2) an exchange of Federal land at the mine for private lands owned by the company in Custer and Bannock counties, Idaho. In response to these proposals and a Section 404 Clean Water Act permit application, 1) the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) will decide whether to approve the portion of the MMPO involving BLM-administered land; 2) the Forest Service will decide whether to approve the portion of the MMPO involving National Forest System land; 3) the US Army Corps of Engineers will decide whether to issue a permit under Section 404 of the Clean Water Act to discharge fill materials into waters of the US as required by the MMPO; 4) the BLM will decide whether to amend the Challis Field Office 1999 resource management plan to identify the BLM-administered land in the land exchange proposal as available for disposal (exchange or sale); and 5) the BLM will decide whether to approve a land disposal action. The final environmental impact statement describes the environmental effects of the two proposals and alternatives to the proposals in a set of MMPO alternatives and an independent set of land disposal alternatives. Alternative M2 (MMPO as submitted) and Alternative L2 (land exchange proposal as submitted) are preferred by the responsible officials
Includes loose errata page

The 2026 Hyundai Boulder Concept is a rugged, body-on-frame SUV debuting at the New York International Auto Show to preview Hyundai's first dedicated off-road platform, with a production truck expected by 2029–2030. It features 37-inch mud-terrain tires, aggressive off-road angles, a unique double-hinged tailgate, and safari windows, signaling a direct competitor to the Ford Bronco and Jeep Wrangler.

Key Concept Specs & Features - Platform: Dedicated body-on-frame architecture. - Powertrain: Potential Extended-Range Electric (EREV) or traditional V6/V8. - Off-Road Equipment: 37-inch mud-terrain tires, high-clearance design, external reservoir shocks, and a part-time 4WD system with a 2-speed transfer case. - Design: Liquid Titanium paint, modular interior with physical switches for trail use, and safari-style fixed roof windows. - Functionality: Double-hinged tailgate opening from either side. - Production Outlook: Midsize truck based on this concept is due by 2029–2030.

97899987.title: File:The Social Security (Working Neighbourhoods) Regulations 2004 (UKSI 2004-959 qp).pdf

ImageDescription.value: These Regulations impose requirements to take part in work-focused interviews (“interviews”) on certain persons who reside in specified areas. The requirements apply to those who make a claim for income support or incapacity benefit or, as at the date that these Regulations come into force, are already entitled to income support except where paragraph 7 (persons incapable of work) of Schedule 1B to the Income Support (General) Regulations 1987 (S.I. 1987-1967) applies.  They also apply to the partners of certain recipients of income support, incapacity benefit, severe disablement allowance or income-based jobseeker’s allowance (other than a joint-claim jobseeker’s allowance) where the recipient is entitled to the benefit at a higher rate in respect of the partner.
